questions.prompt: Net income has grown for three years, while operating cash flow fell close to zero. Which is the best reading?

options.text: Profit is not becoming cash; find out why
options.explanation: Right: this is a warning sign to investigate, with several possible causes.

options.text: Cash flow does not matter if profit grows
options.explanation: No: profit is an accounting figure; cash is what was collected.

questions.prompt: A fictional firm has steady margins and a high return on capital, but trades on a P/E of 70. Which is true?

options.text: A strong business is a good buy at any price
options.explanation: No: the price can assume more than the business delivers.

options.text: A high P/E proves the business is weak
options.explanation: No: a high P/E reflects expectations, not weakness.

options.text: The price assumes a lot of future growth
options.explanation: Right: if growth falls short, the price can drop while the business stays strong.

options.text: It is clearly a bargain at this price
options.explanation: No: low ratios can reflect a shrinking business; it may be cheap for a reason.

options.text: It may be cheap for a reason
options.explanation: Right: falling revenue and a dividend cut explain why buyers pay so little.
No: the yield uses past payments, and this dividend was just cut.
